newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir group seeks role in India, Pakistan talks.
newsitem.headline: Kashmir group seeks role in India, Pakistan talks.

text.p: Kashmir's leading separatist alliance said on Monday it wanted to be included in talks with India and Pakistan to resolve a decades-old dispute over the divided Himalayan region.

"The Hurriyat always believes in peaceful talks provided these are held among all the parties to the dispute with the help of neutral mediators," the All Parties Hurriyat (Freedom) Conference said in a statement.
"All the parties should respect the aspirations of people of Kashmir."
Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral offered on Saturday to hold unconditional talks with separatist rebels to end a seven-year-old insurgency in Kashmir.
But on Sunday Gujral said the guerrillas must lay down their arms first.
The Hurriyat, which bands nearly 30 separatist, religious and political groups, believes India, Pakistan and the Kashmiris should all be included in talks to resolve the Kashmir dispute.
India controls two thirds of the Himalayan region and Pakistan the rest. Both neighbours, who have fought two wars since 1947 over the territory, claim all of Kashmir.

The two archrivals resumed peace talks in March after three years of tense silence. Another round of talks was held in June and a third set is scheduled for September. The Hurriyat was not included in any of the negotiations.

"It is evident from Gujral's offer of talks to mujahideen (fighters) that India is not interested in resolving the Kashmir problem peacefully, and the Hurriyat believes that India wants to suppress the freedom-loving people of Kashmir by military power," the Hurriyat said.

Dozens of guerrilla groups in Kashmir have been fighting since 1990 for merger with Pakistan or independence. Police and hospitals say more than 20,000 people have been killed since the rebellion erupted.
